input.answer:
I can't tell you whether to buy or rent. That depends on your savings, income, how long you'd stay, and your risk tolerance, and it's personal advice, which I don't give. I can share one housing indicator from Statistics Canada, with limits.

Toronto new-home prices (house and land, total) fell over the past year. The index went from 110.4 in 2025-09 to 105.0 in 2026-09. Change: (105.0 − 110.4) / 110.4 = −4.9%. This covers newly built homes only, not resale homes, and it says nothing about rents.

I could not get Toronto rent data. The asking/paid rent table (46-10-0092) was not in the snapshot, and the CMHC rent table (34-10-0133) is annual, ends in 2025, and I could not isolate Toronto from it. For a rent-versus-buy comparison, look at the Statistics Canada asking and paid rent tables, the resale house price data, and mortgage costs. A financial advisor can help you work through your own numbers.

Source: https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/tbl1/en/tv.action?pid=1810020501
